https://blog.playstation.com/2026/07/14/.title: 19 unmissable PS5 games still releasing in 2026
https://blog.playstation.com/2026/07/14/.body:
The future is fantastically bright when it comes to forthcoming games hitting PlayStation 5, with the likes of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Persona 4 Revival due for 2027. Too far out? Don’t worry, we’ve got the perfect tonic of 19 titles that are a bit closer to home, giving you plenty of excuses to get a PS5 now in readiness for the gaming experiences to come.

Halo: Campaign Evolved – July 28

There are a handful of sci-fi classics in gaming, and it’s hard to dispute Halo’s claim among them. Making its PlayStation debut with style, Halo: Campaign Evolved is the ideal introduction to iconic super soldier Master Chief. This Combat Evolved remake comes locked and loaded with upgraded presentation, extra and redesigned missions, and a flood of changes to bring in some of the series’ more popular elements, covering lore, movement, and additional weapons. Not to mention the four-player online co-op, two-player couch co-op, and more.

Beast of Reincarnation – August 4

Personally speaking, there aren’t enough games out there which blend traditional mythology with science fiction, so it’s refreshing to see Game Freak do exactly that with its impressive looking action RPG. Set in the plagued post-apocalyptic ruins of Japan during 4026, blighted outcast Emma and somewhat disturbing canine Koo are humanity’s remaining hope. Seeking out the source of the corruption – the titular Beast of Reincarnation – means exploring a world of mystery, and combining Emma and Koo’s abilities in an intriguing mixture of real time sword-wielding combat and turn-based style commands to unleash the beautiful but blighted pooch.

Big Walk – August 4

It shouldn’t be any surprise that the developer behind Untitled Goose Game has followed it up with a title as wonderfully weird looking as Big Walk. Challenging players to travel through an open world environment might sound a little odd, but when it requires co-op teamwork and communicating via singing, codes, and gesturing by using L2 and R2 to move the characters arms, the charm instantly becomes clear. Up to 12 players can take part in this rather unique puzzle driven, multiplayer only adventure. The game will also be available as part of the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games lineup at launch.

MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls – August 6

Flashy fast-paced fighting, iconic comic book characters, and a vibrant anime-inspired art style? As combos go, Arc System Works’ spectacular tag-based fighter already has the moves to satisfy both fans of the genre and Marvel buffs.

Each of the 20 playable base heroes and villains – ranging from Black Panther and Doctor Doom, to Spider-Man and Carnage – possess unique abilities that makes each of the 4v4 fights an impressive spectacle, for up to 64 players in its online lobby. And don’t worry if you’re new to this type of action, as MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls promises both an intuitive tutorial, a single-player mode that helps you learn more about the mechanics, and the option to make inputs and chain combos easier.

Metal Gear Solid: Collection Master Vol. 2 – August 27

Snake? You bet. Continuing its essential compilation of the legendary stealth series, Konami’s second package brings together Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots, Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, and Metal Gear: Ghost Babel. A fine assortment of slick Snake action, which sneakily packs in a selection of extras and bonuses, including a master book detailing the games’ story and characters, and the ability to receive in-game items if you have any save data stored from Metal Gear Solid: Collection Master Vol. 1.

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy – August 27

A Plague Tale’s intense mixture of action adventure, stealth, and history takes a slightly different route in this third instalment, set 15 years before Requiem. This time developer Asobo Studio puts you in the hands of capable plunderer Sophia in a tale touching on the mythological, as she attempts to survive the deadly traps, puzzles and beasts of Minotaur Island, all while a brutal army gives chase.

Star Wars Zero Company – August 27

Bit Reactor and Respawn Entertainment flipped on the hyperdrive to bring us back to the Clone Wars era for this turn-based tactics title, which means you better get ready for more mercenaries, misfits, and astromechs. This gritty sci-fi strategy features an original tale where you can deploy a team selected from a variety of archetypes, including Jedi and blaster wielding scoundrels, and put them on the battlefield in the valiant mission to keep the galaxy safe. Your deployed troops can also form bonds which unlock devastating combat synergies that might be able to force any issue…

The Blood of Dawnwalker – September 3

Rebel Wolves’ dark fantasy action RPG has been turning heads since its unveiling. But even with the revelation of its expansive choice and consequence system, bloody swords and magic combat, and richly populated 14th-century kingdom of Vale Sangora, there’s still clearly more hiding within its shadowy corners. Vampires both literal and metaphorical bleed against this tale of morals and family, as you’ve given just 30 days to save the family of Coen, who is also dealing with a mysterious variant of the bloodsucking curse.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword – September 4

Capcom’s sword-swinging, soul-stealing, supernatural epic is back. Set in the early Edo period of Kyoto, as lone samurai Musashi you’re tasked with slicing through human enemies and the demonic Genma, using powerful sword stances and extraordinary abilities granted by the legendary Oni Gauntlet. A staggering variety of attacks, parries, and combos are a big feature, but the ability to use the environment during combat to fight dirty is a particularly fun addition.  

Marvel’s Wolverine – September 15

Insomniac Games knows how to make hard-hitting comic book action adventures, so it should be no surprise that one of the most anticipated titles of this year features everyone’s favourite razor-clawed Canadian. This all-new story has Wolverine slicing and dicing his way across the globe to help free his fellow mutants, teaming up with some familiar faces, including Jean Grey, Sabretooth, and Mystique. Brutal combat, unforgettable set pieces and a healing factor that just won’t quit? Sounds about right, bub.

Control Resonant – September 24

Stepping away from the third-person shooter genre of its forbearer, this follow up to Remedy’s popular sci-fi thriller takes its cues from action RPGs. Former Federal Bureau of Control captive Dylan Faden desperately needs to find his sister – and FBC Director – Jesse in order to truly find himself. Wielding his shapeshifting weapon, the Aberrant, to fashion everything from blades to a colossal hammer, Dylan’s quest to help save Manhattan from paranatural annihilation means unnerving enemies, physics defying exploration, and cosmic horror are all certainties.

Silent Hill: Townfall – September 24

Did someone say “unnerving enemies?” A return to Silent Hill is all that and more, as Simon Ordell’s 1996 trek through the Scottish island of St. Amelia throws you into an intimately first-person horror story of loss and consequences. Sure, you have a selection of melee weapons and firearms, but stealth, distractions, and puzzle solving are the only true ways to survive the psychological terrors that await.

Rayman Legends Retold – October 1

Reimagining the fan-favourite action platformer Rayman Legends is a big undertaking, but Ubisoft clearly relishes the challenge with its vibrant 3D visuals, fully voiced cinematics, gameplay tweaks, and additional levels. Fancy bouncing through the Glade of Dreams with up to three of your couch co-op friends? What about a few rounds of the revised football inspired and revamped mini-game Kung Foot?

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve – October 2

Combat flight sims don’t come much more loaded than Bandai Namco’s long-running series. Deadly dogfights partner with first-person cinematic sequences to play out a story which can change based on your actions across the skies. The introduction of an online lobby also signals the largest multiplayer mode of the series to date, with co-op missions, cross-platform play, and up to eight players for competitive combat.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer – October 6

The Star Wars title that took everyone by surprise when it was first unveiled, Galactic Racer has since only gained even more momentum since. Although set in the post Return of the Jedi ‘New Republic’ era, the story driven racing game features characters and customizable vehicles spanning as far back as the prequels, set across planetary favourites such as Jakku and Tatooine. And you can also go for a star lit spin in an online multiplayer mode for up to 12 players, too.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse – October 15

When malevolent forces threaten eternal darkness, House Belmont answers with a wild whip of retribution. This collaboration between Evil Empire, Motion Twin, and Konami blends the smooth action of Dead Cells with the ever-expansive lore and style of Castlevania for a classic side-scrolling adventure full of traps, secrets, and monstrous foes. Set in a besieged medieval Paris and taking place two decades after the events of Castlevania III: Dracula’s Curse and the recent animated series, expect plenty of crafty platforming, spectacular combat, and the constantly surprising level design we all love the series for. 

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 – October 23

The iconic shooter slides a new era into its crosshairs, with its campaign mode set across the Korean Peninsula in a war between North and South Korea. The story’s emotional firefight is flanked by an expansive multiplayer mode of 12 new 6v6 maps, both large and close-quarters – but the new Kill Block map is sure to get the blood pumping, with its constantly changing layouts. Let’s not forget DMZ, where up to 20 squads of up to three players get to duke it out in a living sandbox environment.

Phantom Blade Zero – October 29

Folk horror, fantasy, and wuxia combine for a flashy action RPG featuring fast-paced combat in a dark semi-open world. The fusion of machinery and martial arts inspired by the Golden Age of Hong Kong action films fashions what the developer calls Kungfupunk, as you take an assassin named Soul, who only has 66 days left to live, on a rampaging quest of revenge. Look for a dedicated State of Play coming later this summer. 

Grand Theft Auto VI – November 19

You might have heard of this one. Rockstar Games’ open-world juggernaut is nearly here. We can’t wait to see what awaits Jason and Lucia on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America when the biggest, most immersive evolution of the Grand Theft Auto series yet arrives on November 19.

You probably have even more games which are knocking on the door to be played on your PS5 in the coming months – why not tell us what you’re looking forward to enjoying later this year?

https://blog.playstation.com/2026/06/24/.title: Grand Theft Auto VI plays best on PS5 November 19
https://blog.playstation.com/2026/06/24/.body:
Since Grand Theft Auto first arrived on the original PlayStation in 1997, the series has defined generations of play. We know players are excited for Grand Theft Auto VI, which heads to the state of Leonida — home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond, in the biggest, most expansive evolution of the series yet.  

Thanks to the close partnership between Sony Interactive Entertainment and Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI will play best on PS5 by taking advantage of PS5’s immersive features to deliver a deeply engaging single-player experience when it launches on November 19.

PS5 puts you in the center of the game world with the DualSense wireless controller reacting to your actions and bringing the sights, sounds, and sensations of Jason and Lucia’s story into the palm of your hands. The controller’s haptic feedback offers responsive vibrations, while its adaptive triggers provide dynamic resistance. The controller’s integrated speaker also adds another dimension to key moments and interactions, with sound effects from the controller enhanced by haptic feedback.

With Tempest 3D AudioTech, you can surround yourself in the distinct soundscapes of Leonida. From the streets of Vice City to the moments that unfold all across the state, this highly accurate audio positioning enhances your perception, helping to bring this world to life around you in unmatched ways. Grand Theft Auto VI also leverages the PS5’s ultra-high speed SSD, enabling you to experience the expansive world of Leonida with near-instant load times.

Check out the official Grand Theft Auto VI cover art reveal:

Pre-order at PlayStation Store on June 25

Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI begin June 25 at midnight local time at PlayStation Store, including the Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition, which features an exclusive collection of premium vehicles, weapons, apparel, and action threaded across Jason and Lucia’s story.

Purchases made before November 20 will also include the Vintage Vice City Pack, a collection of items inspired by Vice City’s neon-soaked past. Players who pre-order any edition on PlayStation Store will also receive a redeemable free month of GTA+.

For new players who are looking to jump in, it’s a great chance to also see why PS5 is the best place to play. Players can pick up a PS5 or PS5 Pro at direct.playstation.com (where available) and at local retailers.

Grand Theft Auto VI marks an exciting new chapter for one of gaming’s most iconic series, and we’re proud to help bring the best experience to players on PS5. We can’t wait until the game arrives on November 19 and we look forward to celebrating its launch with Rockstar Games and our PlayStation community around the world. Visit here for more information on Grand Theft Auto VI on PS5.

This all-new story has Wolverine slicing and dicing his way across the globe to help free his fellow mutants, teaming up with some familiar faces, including Jean Grey, Sabretooth, and Mystique. Brutal combat, unforgettable set pieces and a healing factor that just won’t quit? Sounds about right, bub.

Control Resonant – September 24

Stepping away from the third-person shooter genre of its forbearer, this follow up to Remedy’s popular sci-fi thriller takes its cues from action RPGs. Former Federal Bureau of Control captive Dylan Faden desperately needs to find his sister – and FBC Director – Jesse in order to truly find himself. Wielding his shapeshifting weapon, the Aberrant, to fashion everything from blades to a colossal hammer, Dylan’s quest to help save Manhattan from paranatural annihilation means unnerving enemies, physics defying exploration, and cosmic horror are all certainties.

Silent Hill: Townfall – September 24

Did someone say “unnerving enemies?” A return to Silent Hill is all that and more, as Simon Ordell’s 1996 trek through the Scottish island of St. Amelia throws you into an intimately first-person horror story of loss and consequences. Sure, you have a selection of melee weapons and firearms, but stealth, distractions, and puzzle solving are the only true ways to survive the psychological terrors that await.

Rayman Legends Retold – October 1

Reimagining the fan-favourite action platformer Rayman Legends is a big undertaking, but Ubisoft clearly relishes the challenge with its vibrant 3D visuals, fully voiced cinematics, gameplay tweaks, and additional levels. Fancy bouncing through the Glade of Dreams with up to three of your couch co-op friends? What about a few rounds of the revised football inspired and revamped mini-game Kung Foot?

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve – October 2

Combat flight sims don’t come much more loaded than Bandai Namco’s long-running series. Deadly dogfights partner with first-person cinematic sequences to play out a story which can change based on your actions across the skies. The introduction of an online lobby also signals the largest multiplayer mode of the series to date, with co-op missions, cross-platform play, and up to eight players for competitive combat.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer – October 6

The Star Wars title that took everyone by surprise when it was first unveiled, Galactic Racer has since only gained even more momentum since. Although set in the post Return of the Jedi ‘New Republic’ era, the story driven racing game features characters and customizable vehicles spanning as far back as the prequels, set across planetary favourites such as Jakku and Tatooine. And you can also go for a star lit spin in an online multiplayer mode for up to 12 players, too.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse – October 15

When malevolent forces threaten eternal darkness, House Belmont answers with a wild whip of retribution. This collaboration between Evil Empire, Motion Twin, and Konami blends the smooth action of Dead Cells with the ever-expansive lore and style of Castlevania for a classic side-scrolling adventure full of traps, secrets, and monstrous foes. Set in a besieged medieval Paris and taking place two decades after the events of Castlevania III: Dracula’s Curse and the recent animated series, expect plenty of crafty platforming, spectacular combat, and the constantly surprising level design we all love the series for. 

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 – October 23

The iconic shooter slides a new era into its crosshairs, with its campaign mode set across the Korean Peninsula in a war between North and South Korea. The story’s emotional firefight is flanked by an expansive multiplayer mode of 12 new 6v6 maps, both large and close-quarters – but the new Kill Block map is sure to get the blood pumping, with its constantly changing layouts. Let’s not forget DMZ, where up to 20 squads of up to three players get to duke it out in a living sandbox environment.

Phantom Blade Zero – October 29

Folk horror, fantasy, and wuxia combine for a flashy action RPG featuring fast-paced combat in a dark semi-open world. The fusion of machinery and martial arts inspired by the Golden Age of Hong Kong action films fashions what the developer calls Kungfupunk, as you take an assassin named Soul, who only has 66 days left to live, on a rampaging quest of revenge. Look for a dedicated State of Play coming later this summer. 

Grand Theft Auto VI – November 19

You might have heard of this one. Rockstar Games’ open-world juggernaut is nearly here. We can’t wait to see what awaits Jason and Lucia on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America when the biggest, most immersive evolution of the Grand Theft Auto series yet arrives on November 19.

You probably have even more games which are knocking on the door to be played on your PS5 in the coming months – why not tell us what you’re looking forward to enjoying later this year?

If you have spent any time on the streets of LA, you have undoubtedly noticed them: double decker buses wrapped top to bottom with bold messaging, rolling through some of the city’s busiest neighborhoods. It is one of the most eye-catching advertising formats, and there are four (4) reasons it performs so well in a market like Los Angeles.

1) A Format Built for Scale

A double decker gives a brand a massive canvas that towers over street traffic in a way flat stationary ads simply cannot match. In a city as visually saturated as LA, size and height are what make an ad stand out from everything else competing for attention. That scale is a big part of why the format sticks with people long after they have driven or walked past it.

2) LA’s Streets Are Built for It

Los Angeles is a driving city, and its iconic neighborhoods – West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Santa Monica, Downtown LA – are exactly where residents, commuters, and tourists spend their time in traffic. A double decker running fixed routes through those corridors puts a brand in front of the same high-value audience day after day, which is a big part of why the format works here in a way it might not in a less traffic-heavy market.

3) Consistency Makes It Work

Vector Media has been wrapping double deckers across LA for over 15 years, and that experience shows up in how the fleet is run. Vehicles stay newer, cleaner, and better maintained, which means fewer breakdowns and fewer gaps in coverage. Every campaign is on the street 8 hours a day, 7 days a week, running the same fixed routes. That reliability turns a wrapped bus into a format brands can plan a campaign around.

4) Creative Flexibility 

Part of why double decker advertising continues to work is that the creativity does not have to stop at a flat printed wrap. Vector Media’s double decker campaigns can also include:

  • 3D embellishments that add depth and texture to the wrap
  • Illumination so the message pops after dark
  • Extensions that break past the edges of the vehicle entirely

That flexibility gives a brand license to build something that will stop people in their tracks and live on as a memorable ad. 

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does double decker advertising work well in Los Angeles? LA is a driving city with dense traffic through iconic, high-value neighborhoods. A double decker’s large format and fixed routes put a brand in front of the same audience repeatedly, and consistent street time keeps the campaign very visible.

What is a double decker OOH campaign? It is an out-of-home advertising campaign where a double decker bus is wrapped in branded creative and driven along fixed routes, giving a brand a large, mobile, canvas in high-traffic areas.

How long has Vector Media operated double deckers in Los Angeles? Vector Media has operated double decker buses in Los Angeles for over 15 years.

What areas of LA do Vector Media’s double deckers cover? The fleet runs fixed routes through West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Santa Monica, and Downtown LA.

How much street time does a Vector Media double decker campaign guarantee? 8 hours a day, 7 days a week.

Can a double decker wrap include more than print, like lighting or 3D elements? Yes. Vector Media’s double decker campaigns can incorporate 3D embellishments, illumination for nighttime visibility, and physical extensions beyond the vehicle’s edges.

Bringing a Campaign to LA

If you are weighing options for out-of-home in Los Angeles, double deckers are worth a serious look, and the fleet you choose makes a real difference in how that campaign performs. https://vectormedia.com/5-steps-to-ownin.title: 5 Steps to Owning Conference Season in New York and San Francisco
https://vectormedia.com/5-steps-to-ownin.body:
Conference season is back, and two cities are about to feel it. Every fall, New York becomes a destination for Advertising Week, Climate Week, Fashion Week to name a few. At the same time San Francisco hosts Dreamforce and TechCrunch Disrupt, among other AI / Tech conferences.

For brands, the challenge isn’t finding an audience, it’s finding a way to break through the noise. Yet, attendees move in predictable, concentrated patterns: hotel to convention center, convention center to the after-party, one crowded sidewalk block after another. So the key is to build a campaign that moves with that flow, and becomes part of the experience.

Step 1: Understand Who You’re Talking To

A conference crowd isn’t a general market. It’s a dense, high-intent, short-window audience that’s already primed to focus on a specific category. They’re checking Slack between sessions, comparing notes over coffee, and posting from the show floor in real time. A campaign that meets attendees in that headspace, at the moment they’re gathered, will get attention that a standard media buy simply won’t.

Step 2: Put a Double Decker on the Route

In Manhattan, wrap a Double Decker bus and circulate it through the Javits Center corridor, Times Square, and Penn Station area during Advertising Week. These moving canvases won’t be missed. Attendees will see it on the way to the keynote, again at lunch, and again heading to happy hour. That repetition builds the kind of recall you want.

In San Francisco, run the same format along the Moscone corridor during Dreamforce, where foot and rideshare traffic funnels tightly around South of Market (SoMa) for days at a time. A Double Decker wrap turns that predictable congestion into a predictable advantage.

Step 3: Brand the Commute With a Custom Coach Bus

Conference attendees spend a surprising amount of their week in transit: airport shuttles, hotel-to-venue runs, off-site dinner transport. Wrap a coach bus and put your brand in that in-between time, when attendees are taking a seat and a breath. 

For a brand willing to go further, sponsor the actual shuttle service for the conference. Wrap the exterior and the interior, and give conference goers a water or a treat. Turn necessary logistics into a moment of appreciation. 

Step 4: Use LED Trucks to Hit Peak Moments

LED trucks have the luxury of being at the right place at the right time. Park one outside the venue entrance during badge pickup. Circle around the block during a keynote’s break. Reposition it for an evening event across town. That flexibility matters most during conference week, when the highest-value moments – a big keynote letting out, a happy hour starting – are known in advance but only last for a short time. LED trucks can be wherever the center of attention moves to next.

Step 5: Add a Coffee Truck for Goodwill

Not everything needs to be big to be effective. Station a branded coffee truck outside a conference venue during the morning rush. It solves a real need for a tired attendee and creates a warm, low-friction brand interaction, the kind of activation that gets photographed and shared without anyone asking for it to be. People remember who handed them a coffee before their 9 a.m. panel.

 

Key Takeaway

During conference season, a winning strategy is knowing who you are talking to, building a campaign that moves with the flow, and having your brand become part of the experience.

https://vectormedia.com/marketing-in-mot.title: Marketing in Motion: How Studios Build Buzz Before Opening Day
https://vectormedia.com/marketing-in-mot.body:
When a studio has a release date on the calendar, the countdown isn’t just creative, it’s logistical. Trailers drop, press junkets ramp up, and marketing teams start asking the same question: how do we get in front of audiences everywhere they already are, in the weeks right before opening weekend?

For entertainment marketers, out-of-home advertising has become one of the most effective answers. Movies are visual, emotional, and made for a big canvas, and nothing puts a film in front of a city the way transit and street-level media can. But the real advantage isn’t just going big in one place. It’s showing up in multiple markets, through multiple formats, all at once.

The Dino Movie Takes Over Five Cities

One of the best examples of this playing out right now is the campaign behind Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie. With the film headed to theaters August 14th, Paramount is sending the pups on a five-city adventure across Los Angeles, New York City, Dallas, Houston, and Chicago in the weeks leading up to release.

The campaign leans on exactly the kind of format mix that makes a launch feel like an event rather than a single ad buy. Double decker buses wrapped in Dino Movie creative roll through Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, and New York City. Dallas gets its own signature touch with a fully wrapped trolley. Los Angeles adds another layer with static and digital shelters, plus an immersive custom shelter build out complete with a jungle foliage and larger-than-life 3D dinosaur, giving the pups a presence at street level as well as on the road. Same characters, same countdown to release day, but a different touchpoint depending on where a family happens to cross paths with the campaign.

This is the kind of activation Vector Media helps bring to life. Here’s why it works.

 

Double Deckers: Movement Meets Memorability

Wrapped vehicles do something static media can’t: they travel through busy downtown corridors, business districts, and tourist hot spots all in the same day. In Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, and New York City, double decker buses wrapped in Dino Movie creative turn the vehicle itself into a rolling piece of movie marketing, seen by pedestrians, drivers, and riders alike, in a way that feels like a hometown parade rather than an ad.

Trolleys: A Local Signature

Dallas gets its own standout moment with a fully wrapped trolley. Trolleys carry a built-in sense of place, they’re already a familiar sight downtown, which makes wrapping one in movie creative feel less like an intrusion and more like a local event. It’s a format that rewards a single market with a distinctive, photogenic touch.

Static and Digital Shelters, Plus Build Outs: Owning the Street Level

In Los Angeles, the campaign goes a step further with static and digital shelters alongside a fully custom shelter build out. The design turns the shelter roofline into a jungle canopy, with lush greenery spilling over the top, baby dinosaurs peeking out from the leaves, and an oversized dino head rising up behind the branded Dino Movie logo. The ad panels beneath carry the full cast and theatrical release date, so riders get both the spectacle up top and the campaign details at eye level. It’s the kind of build out that turns a bus stop into a photo opportunity, and gives the pups a presence that’s hard to walk past without noticing.

Why Five Cities Beats One

Coordinating the Dino Movie tour across LA, New York, Dallas, Houston, and Chicago isn’t just about reach, it’s about relevance. Each of those cities has its own transit culture, its own commuter patterns, and its own mix of families, tourists, and daily riders. A national release benefits from feeling local in each of those places at the same time, which is exactly what a coordinated, multi-market OOH buy delivers.

Picture a double decker rolling past commuters on their way to school in Chicago, another one greeting tourists in New York City, a wrapped trolley turning heads in downtown Dallas, and a jungle-canopy shelter build out stopping foot traffic on a busy Los Angeles corner. Different cities, different formats, all building toward the same August 14th release date, and all bringing a little bit of coast-to-coast smiles along the way.

Building the Right Mix for Your Release

No two entertainment campaigns need the exact same formula. Some releases benefit from heavy digital presence for last-minute flexibility. Others lean into vehicle wraps for maximum visual impact in high-traffic corridors. The right mix depends on the film, the audience, and the timeline leading up to opening day.

That’s where a media partner with reach across 45+ markets and a full range of formats makes the difference, helping studios and distributors build a campaign that feels present everywhere, not just visible in one place.

Whether it’s a five-city tour like the one carrying the pups toward their August 14th release or a hyperlocal push in a single market, the goal is the same: put the film in front of audiences in the real world, in the moments right before they decide what to see this weekend.

The Hamptons is one of the hardest markets in the country to advertise in, and that’s exactly what makes it valuable. Nassau and Suffolk County restrictions eliminate most traditional out-of-home options along the route east, which means brands need a partner who already holds the access. Vector Media’s exclusive partnership with the Hampton Jitney, paired with in-house experiential activations, is currently the only way for a brand to reach the Hamptons audience at scale, and that reach extends well past the riders themselves, to the foot traffic in high-end Manhattan neighborhoods along the route and to everyone else traveling to and from the Hamptons.

 

Why the Hampton Jitney Is the Only OOH Option Between the Midtown Tunnel and Montauk

Advertising restrictions in Nassau and Suffolk counties limit large-format out-of-home media along the expressway corridor leading into the Hamptons. The result: the Hampton Jitney is one of the only out-of-home advertising options between the Midtown Tunnel and Montauk.

Of the ways to get to the Hamptons (helicopter, car, train, or bus), the Jitney is the most accessible mass-transit option and draws a more affluent rider than any of the others. Hampton Jitney has connected NYC to the East End for more than 50 years, running through Midtown, the Upper East Side, the Long Island Expressway, and into the Hamptons itself. It provides single placement exposure in both the city and the Hamptons.

Hampton Jitney Advertising Formats

Vector’s partnership with Hampton Jitney covers the full fleet and the full rider experience, not just the exterior of the bus:

  • Exterior bus wraps across the Jitney’s luxury coach fleet
  • Interior advertisements placed throughout the cabin
  • Digital screens onboard
  • Onboard Wi-Fi sponsorships, including a branded splash page, dynamic landing page, email opt-ins, and social log-ins
  • Onboard sampling
  • Pop-up event sponsorships

Who You’re Reaching

The Hampton Jitney’s ridership skews upscale by design. Riders are largely Manhattan professionals and second-home owners making the trip east, a captive audience for the length of the ride, whether that’s a summer weekender heading out on a Friday or a mid-week commuter. The Jitney draws the most accessible, affluent segment of that traveler base.

The reach doesn’t stop at the riders. The exterior of the bus is a moving billboard, seen by foot traffic and drivers throughout the high-end Manhattan neighborhoods the Jitney passes through on its route, and by anyone else on the road traveling to or from the Hamptons. A brand on the Jitney is in front of the rider, the pedestrian on the sidewalk, and the driver in the next lane, all on the same trip.

Brands that have branded Hampton Jitney fleets during peak summer months have done so for the same reason: the route puts a message in front of the audience in the city before they even reach the East End, covering the full trip rather than just the destination.

Experiential Activations: Beyond the Bus Wrap

Media placement gets a brand seen. Experiential gets a brand felt. Vector’s in-house experiential team builds ground-up brand activations that pair with Hamptons transit media rather than standing apart from it, including:

  • Custom vehicle builds, like Vector’s Looking Glass, a glass-sided vehicle designed for product showcases and walk-in brand experiences
  • Pop-up events tied to Jitney stops or Hamptons summer calendar moments
  • Product sampling and distribution, giving consumers a first physical interaction with the brand
  • Custom fabrication and immersive builds, from modular structures to fully branded vehicle fleets
  • Data-backed measurement, so activations are optimized against real audience response, not just impressions

The pairing matters. A Jitney wrap builds awareness across the entire route from Manhattan to Montauk. An activation at the destination, or at a Hamptons event tied to that same brand, converts that awareness into an actual interaction. Vector’s experiential and transit teams work from the same brand brief, so the bus and the activation reinforce a single campaign rather than running as separate efforts.

Why This Combination Works for Luxury and Lifestyle Brands

Brands that succeed in the Hamptons tend to share a few traits: high household income targets, a short seasonal window to make an impression, and a need to be remembered past Labor Day. The Jitney solves reach within a legally restricted media market. Experiential solves recall by giving the audience something to do, sample, or walk into, not just something to glance at. Together, they cover a full-funnel path from a bus wrap seen on the LIE to a branded activation at a Hamptons event that same weekend.

FAQ: Advertising in the Hamptons

A double decker gives a brand a massive canvas that towers over street traffic in a way flat stationary ads simply cannot match. 2) LA’s Streets Are Built for It

Los Angeles is a driving city, and its iconic neighborhoods – West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Santa Monica, Downtown LA – are exactly where residents, commuters, and tourists spend their time in traffic. A double decker running fixed routes through those corridors puts a brand in front of the same high-value audience day after day, which is a big part of why the format works here in a way it might not in a less traffic-heavy market.

3) Consistency Makes It Work

Vector Media has been wrapping double deckers across LA for over 15 years, and that experience shows up in how the fleet is run. Every campaign is on the street 8 hours a day, 7 days a week, running the same fixed routes. That reliability turns a wrapped bus into a format brands can plan a campaign around.

4) Creative Flexibility 

Part of why double decker advertising continues to work is that the creativity does not have to stop at a flat printed wrap. Vector Media’s double decker campaigns can also include:

That flexibility gives a brand license to build something that will stop people in their tracks and live on as a memorable ad.

https://vectormedia.com/5-steps-to-ownin.title: 5 Steps to Owning Conference Season in New York and San Francisco
https://vectormedia.com/5-steps-to-ownin.body:
Conference season is back, and two cities are about to feel it. Every fall, New York becomes a destination for Advertising Week, Climate Week, Fashion Week to name a few. At the same time San Francisco hosts Dreamforce and TechCrunch Disrupt, among other AI / Tech conferences.

For brands, the challenge isn’t finding an audience, it’s finding a way to break through the noise. Yet, attendees move in predictable, concentrated patterns: hotel to convention center, convention center to the after-party, one crowded sidewalk block after another. So the key is to build a campaign that moves with that flow, and becomes part of the experience.

Step 1: Understand Who You’re Talking To

A conference crowd isn’t a general market. It’s a dense, high-intent, short-window audience that’s already primed to focus on a specific category. They’re checking Slack between sessions, comparing notes over coffee, and posting from the show floor in real time. A campaign that meets attendees in that headspace, at the moment they’re gathered, will get attention that a standard media buy simply won’t.

Step 2: Put a Double Decker on the Route

In Manhattan, wrap a Double Decker bus and circulate it through the Javits Center corridor, Times Square, and Penn Station area during Advertising Week. These moving canvases won’t be missed. Attendees will see it on the way to the keynote, again at lunch, and again heading to happy hour. That repetition builds the kind of recall you want.

In San Francisco, run the same format along the Moscone corridor during Dreamforce, where foot and rideshare traffic funnels tightly around South of Market (SoMa) for days at a time. A Double Decker wrap turns that predictable congestion into a predictable advantage.

Step 3: Brand the Commute With a Custom Coach Bus

Conference attendees spend a surprising amount of their week in transit: airport shuttles, hotel-to-venue runs, off-site dinner transport. Wrap a coach bus and put your brand in that in-between time, when attendees are taking a seat and a breath. 

For a brand willing to go further, sponsor the actual shuttle service for the conference. Wrap the exterior and the interior, and give conference goers a water or a treat. Turn necessary logistics into a moment of appreciation. 

Step 4: Use LED Trucks to Hit Peak Moments

LED trucks have the luxury of being at the right place at the right time. Park one outside the venue entrance during badge pickup. Circle around the block during a keynote’s break. Reposition it for an evening event across town. That flexibility matters most during conference week, when the highest-value moments – a big keynote letting out, a happy hour starting – are known in advance but only last for a short time. LED trucks can be wherever the center of attention moves to next.

Step 5: Add a Coffee Truck for Goodwill

Not everything needs to be big to be effective. Station a branded coffee truck outside a conference venue during the morning rush. It solves a real need for a tired attendee and creates a warm, low-friction brand interaction, the kind of activation that gets photographed and shared without anyone asking for it to be. People remember who handed them a coffee before their 9 a.m. panel.

 

Key Takeaway

During conference season, a winning strategy is knowing who you are talking to, building a campaign that moves with the flow, and having your brand become part of the experience.

https://vectormedia.com/marketing-in-mot.title: Marketing in Motion: How Studios Build Buzz Before Opening Day
https://vectormedia.com/marketing-in-mot.body:
When a studio has a release date on the calendar, the countdown isn’t just creative, it’s logistical. Trailers drop, press junkets ramp up, and marketing teams start asking the same question: how do we get in front of audiences everywhere they already are, in the weeks right before opening weekend?

For entertainment marketers, out-of-home advertising has become one of the most effective answers. Movies are visual, emotional, and made for a big canvas, and nothing puts a film in front of a city the way transit and street-level media can. But the real advantage isn’t just going big in one place. It’s showing up in multiple markets, through multiple formats, all at once.

The Dino Movie Takes Over Five Cities

One of the best examples of this playing out right now is the campaign behind Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie. With the film headed to theaters August 14th, Paramount is sending the pups on a five-city adventure across Los Angeles, New York City, Dallas, Houston, and Chicago in the weeks leading up to release.

The campaign leans on exactly the kind of format mix that makes a launch feel like an event rather than a single ad buy. Double decker buses wrapped in Dino Movie creative roll through Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, and New York City. Dallas gets its own signature touch with a fully wrapped trolley. Los Angeles adds another layer with static and digital shelters, plus an immersive custom shelter build out complete with a jungle foliage and larger-than-life 3D dinosaur, giving the pups a presence at street level as well as on the road. Same characters, same countdown to release day, but a different touchpoint depending on where a family happens to cross paths with the campaign.

This is the kind of activation Vector Media helps bring to life. Here’s why it works.

 

Double Deckers: Movement Meets Memorability

Wrapped vehicles do something static media can’t: they travel through busy downtown corridors, business districts, and tourist hot spots all in the same day. In Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, and New York City, double decker buses wrapped in Dino Movie creative turn the vehicle itself into a rolling piece of movie marketing, seen by pedestrians, drivers, and riders alike, in a way that feels like a hometown parade rather than an ad.

Trolleys: A Local Signature

Dallas gets its own standout moment with a fully wrapped trolley. Trolleys carry a built-in sense of place, they’re already a familiar sight downtown, which makes wrapping one in movie creative feel less like an intrusion and more like a local event. It’s a format that rewards a single market with a distinctive, photogenic touch.

Static and Digital Shelters, Plus Build Outs: Owning the Street Level

In Los Angeles, the campaign goes a step further with static and digital shelters alongside a fully custom shelter build out. The design turns the shelter roofline into a jungle canopy, with lush greenery spilling over the top, baby dinosaurs peeking out from the leaves, and an oversized dino head rising up behind the branded Dino Movie logo. The ad panels beneath carry the full cast and theatrical release date, so riders get both the spectacle up top and the campaign details at eye level. It’s the kind of build out that turns a bus stop into a photo opportunity, and gives the pups a presence that’s hard to walk past without noticing.

Why Five Cities Beats One

Coordinating the Dino Movie tour across LA, New York, Dallas, Houston, and Chicago isn’t just about reach, it’s about relevance. Each of those cities has its own transit culture, its own commuter patterns, and its own mix of families, tourists, and daily riders. A national release benefits from feeling local in each of those places at the same time, which is exactly what a coordinated, multi-market OOH buy delivers.

Picture a double decker rolling past commuters on their way to school in Chicago, another one greeting tourists in New York City, a wrapped trolley turning heads in downtown Dallas, and a jungle-canopy shelter build out stopping foot traffic on a busy Los Angeles corner. Different cities, different formats, all building toward the same August 14th release date, and all bringing a little bit of coast-to-coast smiles along the way.

Building the Right Mix for Your Release

No two entertainment campaigns need the exact same formula. Some releases benefit from heavy digital presence for last-minute flexibility. Others lean into vehicle wraps for maximum visual impact in high-traffic corridors. The right mix depends on the film, the audience, and the timeline leading up to opening day.

That’s where a media partner with reach across 45+ markets and a full range of formats makes the difference, helping studios and distributors build a campaign that feels present everywhere, not just visible in one place.

Whether it’s a five-city tour like the one carrying the pups toward their August 14th release or a hyperlocal push in a single market, the goal is the same: put the film in front of audiences in the real world, in the moments right before they decide what to see this weekend.
